assessment: The shift is documented, not judged. Against the pre-switch path the bundle score falls by 0.63 (1.4 %), of which 0.54 comes from the recipe switch and 0.09 from the encodings; sea surface temperature and column water get worse, winds, pressure, rain and currents better, and the whole world is 1.2 C cooler because of the recipe switch. Without a repeat run these differences cannot be separated from run-to-run noise. Whether run 385 is an acceptable baseline is the user's visual verdict.
lessons: Geosphere and land-hydrosphere fields keep integer types: every producer is integer (uint16 terrain imports, the engine's uint16 datum, legacy integer algorithms), so their type can change later without a new baseline. Category codes stay int16 for the same reason.

atmosphere.precipitation and atmosphere.precipitation_exact are both float now and differ only where the legacy January/July passes adjust rain; the legacy-to-seasonal sync overwrites one and not the other.

Accepted meaning changes of the exact readers: the transition-season fallback of syncseasonalclimatefromlegacy no longer truncates, and a stored SST between -0.5 and 0.5 C no longer counts as unset in pressuresurfacetemperature.

Seen in pre-switch and baseline alike: a precipitation hotspot at the north pole near 87 E, a one-row line along the equator in January column water and convergence, staircase blocks in 850 hPa wind over high terrain, a sharp line along the Antarctic coast in surface wind.

assessment: The bundle evaluation reproduces the legacy ranking and seven of eleven field losses exactly; the four wind and pressure losses differ by 0.5 to 1.3 percent through their inputs, and the total by 0.06 of 43. The legacy chain can retire. Run 385 is reproduced bit for bit, so score differences between runs of the same binary are not noise. lessons: A repeat of the climate baseline is bit-identical; any score difference between two runs of one binary comes from the options.
--climate-transport mpdata takes about five times as long as ffsl at the registered settings and changes global-balanced-v1 by +0.025.
weighted_relative_error (registry) and global-balanced-v1 can order a pair of runs differently.
